extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, state plan developers, regulated owners/operators of affected EGUs, and stakeholders commenting on EPA emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Designing or evaluating state implementation plans under the EPA's emission guidelines for affected electric generating units (EGUs), including allowable compliance flexibilities (averaging, trading, unit-specific mass limits) and required demonstration of equivalence to unit-specific rate-based standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF use and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: RULOF provisions are intended for EGUs in unique circumstances and may result in less stringent standards (different BSER basis, longer compliance schedule, or combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because RULOF-based, bespoke standards create uncertainty about how states will particularize compliance obligations and future utilization, EPA prohibits RULOF sources from using unit-specific mass-based compliance and is concerned that allowing RULOF sources to participate in trading/averaging could undermine state plan stringency by incentivizing other, more stringent sources to underperform (obtain compliance instruments from RULOF sources or average with them). The bespoke nature of RULOF makes it difficult for EPA to provide mass-based compliance principles that ensure equivalent emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories from averaging/trading and unit-specific mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories do not require improvement in emission performance (per BSER) and already account for variable efficiency across operating levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded these sources are unlikely to overperform and therefore their participation in emission trading or averaging would add little value and could undermine equivalence by incentivizing other sources to underperform. Accordingly, affected EGUs in these subcategories are not permitted to use unit-specific mass-based compliance and EPA discourages their inclusion in trading/averaging programs because it may reduce the incentive for sources to operate more cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of coal-fired subcategories to use compliance flexibilities (within parameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medium- and long-term coal-fired subcategories are permitted to participate in averaging, trading, and unit-specific mass-based compliance within EPA-set parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA allows coal-fired EGUs to use compliance flexibilities because overperformance is possible and incentivizable (and because IRC section 45Q may incentivize CCS for long-term units). EPA is not finalizing a restriction on trading/averaging across the two coal subcategories (medium-term may trade/average with long-term), subject to the specific constraints and safeguards described in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for rate-based averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate-based averaging is permissible only for affected EGUs in the medium- and long-term coal-fired subcategories and only at the facility level or the owner/operator level within a single state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA limits averaging to facility or owner/operator-within-state scope because broader averaging (across owners/operators, states, or interstate) would create prohibitive complexity and hinder transparency and timely compliance tracking. If a state wants a broader (statewide/interstate) rate-based compliance flexibility, it must implement rate-based trading instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan contents required for rate-based averaging demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: A state plan that adopts rate-based averaging must specify the participating group of affected EGUs, the unit-specific rate-based presumptive standard of performance applicable to each participating EGU, and the aggregate compliance rate and its calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For owner/operator-level averaging, plans must include self-executing provisions addressing changes in owner/operator during program implementation so plan revision is not required. Only affected EGUs may be included in both the aggregate rate calculation and the aggregate compliance demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output-basis (gross generation) weighting requirement for averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: The aggregate compliance rate for rate-based averaging must be a gross generation-based weighted average of the required standards of performance of each participating affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requires output-basis weighting to ensure the aggregate compliance rate is representative of unit-specific standards and to preserve equivalence with unit-specific rate-based implementation. Commenters generally supported this calculation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based trading instrument denomination and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a rate-based trading program, the tradable compliance instrument must be denominated in one ton of CO2 and compliance instruments awarded equal the difference between an EGU's standard and its actual reported CO2 emission rate multiplied by gross generation (MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denominating instruments in MWh (or another unit) is unacceptable because such units are not fungible across EGUs with different lb CO2/MWh rates. Awards are issued annually based on under-rate performance; surrender of instruments is accounted for in the numerator (total annual CO2 emissions) of an EGU's CO2 emission rate when demonstrating compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence demonstration requirements for rate-based trading/averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: States must demonstrate equivalence to unit-specific, rate-based standards by specifying participating EGUs, the applicable individual standards, and how compliance will be demonstrated (reported performance plus surrender of instruments where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA emphasizes rate-based trading/averaging must be designed to maintain an equivalent level of emission reduction over time. Rate-based trading is less reliant on future utilization assumptions (utilization is inherently accounted for) and therefore is considered more certain than mass-based approaches for preserving equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-specific mass-based compliance must include a backstop emission rate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state uses unit-specific mass-based compliance, the mass limit must be accompanied by a unit-specific backstop emission rate (expressed in lb CO2/MWh gross) for compliance demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requires a backstop rate because these emission guidelines focus on cleaner unit-specific performance (rates), and mass limits alone rely on utilization assumptions which can be uncertain. The backstop rate helps ensure units operate more cleanly and that emission reductions required under CAA section 111 are achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based approach for long-term coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired EGUs (installing CCS), EPA provides a presumptively approvable method: mass limit = presumptively approvable rate × gross generation at an assumed annual capacity factor of 80%; require a backstop emission rate equivalent to an 80% reduction relative to baseline on an annual calendar-year basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considers 90% capture achievable over a year for CCS but adopts 80% capacity factor (used in BSER analysis) for establishing mass limits consistent with the IRC section 45Q incentive. States may deviate from this presumptively approvable approach but deviations must include a backstop rate and will be reviewed for reasonableness (e.g., historic capacity factor data over 8 continuous quarters). EPA believes this approach preserves equivalent emission reductions due to the high stringency of the subcategory and the 45Q incentive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based approach for medium-term coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing a presumptively approvable mass-based compliance approach for medium-term coal-fired EGUs because of uncertainty in future utilization and the relatively low stringency (16% reduction) of the subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may nonetheless allow unit-specific mass-based compliance at their discretion, but for plan approval they must (1) apply a backstop rate in conjunction with any mass limit (EPA suggests a starting backstop of roughly 14.5% reduction relative to baseline based on proportional scaling) and (2) demonstrate that the plan would achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction, including showing how the mass limit was calculated and the basis for utilization assumptions. EPA will apply a high degree of scrutiny to utilization assumptions because errors can render mass limits non-binding or otherwise less stringent than unit-specific rate-based requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-based emission trading design and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include mass-based emission trading for medium- and long-term coal-fired EGUs, but the same caveats as unit-specific mass-based compliance apply: a unit-specific backstop rate is required and the mass budget must be based on rate-based standards plus assumed utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish a mass budget, states convert unit-specific rate-based standards to mass limits using assumed utilization for each participating EGU and sum to an aggregate budget. The plan must specify how allowances (each equal to one ton CO2) are distributed and surrendered. Each participating EGU must also demonstrate compliance with the unit-specific backstop rate. EPA expresses concern that compounding uncertainty from multiple participating sources makes appropriate mass budget calculation difficult, and will scrutinize designs to ensure equivalence to unit-specific rate-based standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on relying on non-affected sources and requirement to ensure equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must ensure an equivalent level of emission reduction from the sources that are 'affected' under these emission guidelines and cannot rely on or account for emission reductions at non-affected sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing mass-based or rate-based compliance flexibilities, states should consult EPA sections on stringency and demonstrating equivalence (e.g., X.B and X.D.1) and include required design features (backstop rates, calculation bases, documentation) so EPA can review and approve the plan. EPA will closely review deviations from presumptive approaches.
